newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says Mideast summit failed, wants Arab action.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Mideast summit failed, wants Arab action.

text.p: Syria on Thursday dismissed Washington's Middle East summit as a failure and urged Arab states to cut ties with Israel to force it to accept Arab demands for peace.
"Washington's summit has totally failed to find any solution for the existing disputes between the Palestinians and the Israelis," the official daily al-Baath said.

"Arabs should not waste time waiting for any gesture from (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's government.. they should sever ties with Israel and freeze the multilateral talks," it said in a comment signed by its director-general Turky Saqr.

U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday at the end of the summit which he called to prevent the collapse of the Middle East peace process that Palestinians and Israelis would resume talks on Sunday.
Fifty-eight Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in five days of clashes after Israel opened a tunnel to archaeological sites near Jerusalem's temple mount, sacred to Moslems and Jews.

"Netanyahu wanted the Washington summit to adopt his style of negotiations based on nothing for Arabs. He wanted the Washington summit to reward the aggressor for killing his victim and endorsing his occupation of Arab lands and opening tunnels..," al-Baath said.
Syria and Arab states have strongly condemned Netanyahu's policy of rejecting any trade of occupied Arab lands for peace and refusing the establishment of a Palestinian state.

Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but no negotiations have been conducted since the election of Netanyahu as prime minister on May 29. Damascus wants Israel to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights captured by Israel in 1967.
